intro: 39 Robinson Road is the refurbished former Robinson Point in the CBD, reported to complete in 2026. Tenants taking space in a refurbished building should plan their fit-out around what the refurbishment has upgraded and what it has kept. Below: key facts, what tenants usually change, a handover check and how to plan a 39 Robinson Road fit-out or renovation.

sections.heading: What to know about 39 Robinson Road
sections.text:
In a refurbished office building the core services are usually upgraded, but floor plates, columns and window lines often stay as they were. A fit-out that works with those fixed points, rather than against them, costs less and gets approved faster.

CBD tenants often move on a tight timeline between leases. Ask the landlord for the fit-out guidelines and the handover condition early, so your design starts from what will actually be on site.

sections.heading: What tenants usually change
bullets: Layouts planned around existing columns and window lines.
Glass meeting rooms that keep daylight in the open office.
Pantry and collaboration areas for hybrid teams.
Data and power planned for flexible desks.
Acoustic treatment for meeting rooms and phone booths.

timeline_note: A typical office fit-out takes about 8 to 16 weeks from brief to move-in, including landlord submissions and any fire safety approvals.

faq.q: When will 39 Robinson Road be ready?
faq.a: EdgeProp reported an expected TOP in 2026. We could not confirm this on an official page, so check with the landlord for your handover date.

faq.q: What should we ask the landlord before designing?
faq.a: The fit-out guidelines, the handover condition of the space, the approved working hours, and the submissions they need before work starts.
Only if the works change fire safety items such as sprinklers, alarms or escape routes. These need a qualified person and SCDF's approval.
